question: How large must the numerical parameters of explicit neural-network approximants become as approximation accuracy improves, beyond counting their width, depth, or nonzero weights?

key_findings.claim: A modified near-optimal deep-ReLU construction approximates C^q functions with polynomially bounded parameter magnitudes.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 4 preserves uniform error of order N^(-2q/d)L^(-2q/d) with width O(N log N), increases depth from the precursor's O(L log L) to O(L^2 log L), and bounds the largest realizing parameter by O(max(N^((6q-3)/d)L^((6q-2)/d), NL(N+L^2))). The proof tracks scale factors through explicit projection, monomial, derivative-fitting, multiplication, and median subnetworks.

key_findings.claim: The result is an existence upper bound for one explicit realization, not a lower bound or optimal characterization of required weights.
key_findings.evidence: The paper defines P(network) as the minimum infinity norm across parameterizations realizing the same function, but bounds it by exhibiting a particular parameter vector. The authors explicitly state they make no claim that the asymptotic parameter growth is optimal. ReLU rescaling symmetries and alternative constructions could yield smaller magnitudes.

key_findings.claim: The claimed advantage over existing parameter-growth bounds is conditional on activation, regularity, metric, and complexity normalization.
key_findings.evidence: Tables 1-2 convert different results to normalized width or nonzero-weight counts and compare exponent bounds. The new ReLU bound is slower-growing in most enumerated regimes and always favorable in the paper's high-dimensional comparison, but ReQU already permits uniformly bounded parameters with a slightly different error/regularity tradeoff. Log factors and the extra quadratic depth must be restored for an implementation-level comparison.

key_findings.claim: A shallow Gaussian/logistic construction can require exponentially growing parameters, but this is not an impossibility theorem for all shallow smooth-activation networks.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 2 analyzes the specific Mhaskar trigonometric-polynomial approximation for one W^{1,infinity} target and proves Omega(c^m) realizing coefficients for Gaussian or logistic activations under stated derivative/Fourier conditions. Remarks extend the target class, yet the conclusion remains construction-specific and does not show every shallow approximation of those functions needs exponential weights.

key_findings.claim: The work connects approximation magnitude to generalization/training error analyses only indirectly.
key_findings.evidence: The motivation notes that empirical-risk and random-initialization bounds depend on an a priori parameter box, so explicit polynomial growth can be substituted into such analyses. No optimizer is shown to find the constructed weights, no numerical-conditioning or finite-precision experiment is run, and the approximants are not evaluated empirically.

method.core_idea: Audit an explicit optimal-order ReLU approximation proof component by component and bound the infinity norm of all realizing weights as width and depth grow.
method.mechanism: Track parameter scales through Taylor-cell projection, polynomial/multiplication modules, derivative-value encoding, and a median extension across trifling regions; modify a depth-sensitive module to avoid exponential coefficients.
assumptions: The target lies in C^q([0,1]^d) with bounded derivatives.
Approximation is measured uniformly on a compact cube.
Width and depth parameters N,L grow through the specified constructive architecture.
Maximum absolute parameter is an informative numerical-complexity measure despite ReLU reparameterization symmetries.

techniques.role: Measures the smallest maximum parameter among equivalent realizations.
Bounds weights through every composed approximation subnetwork.
Approximates smooth functions cellwise using fitted derivatives and multiplication networks.
Extends a cellwise approximation uniformly across cell boundaries.

evaluations.setting: C^q functions on [0,1]^d, explicit deep ReLU approximants
evaluations.metric: Uniform approximation error and maximum absolute parameter
evaluations.result: Error O(N^(-2q/d)L^(-2q/d)) with polynomial parameter growth and O(N log N) by O(L^2 log L) architecture
evaluations.baseline: The Lu-Shen-Yang-Zhang construction without an explicit polynomial parameter audit

evaluations.setting: Normalized comparison by width or number of nonzero weights
evaluations.metric: Exponent of approximation and parameter growth
evaluations.result: The paper's bound improves most compared regimes but not uniformly bounded ReQU weights
evaluations.baseline: Tanh, sigmoid, encodable-weight, and ReQU approximation results

evaluations.setting: Specific shallow Mhaskar approximants with Gaussian/logistic activations
evaluations.result: At least Omega(c^m) for the analyzed target/construction
evaluations.baseline: Polynomial growth in the modified deep-ReLU construction

limitations: Author-stated: optimality of the parameter-growth upper bound is not established.
Reviewer-identified: the construction increases depth quadratically in L relative to the approximation-rate precursor.
Reviewer-identified: comparisons combine activations and regularity classes and suppress logarithmic factors, so there is no universal dominance statement.
Reviewer-identified: no finite-precision, trainability, or empirical conditioning consequence is tested.
Reviewer-identified: exponential shallow growth applies to a particular constructive scheme, not all shallow Gaussian/logistic approximants.
failure_modes: A theoretically polynomial maximum weight can still be numerically enormous at useful dimension and smoothness.
The explicit approximant may be inaccessible to gradient-based training.
Uniform high-dimensional rates retain the curse-of-dimensionality exponent q/d.
Alternative ReLU rescalings can make raw maximum-weight comparisons representation-dependent.
Finite precision may invalidate exact projection and narrow-cell constructions before asymptotic error is reached.
reusable_insights: Approximation theorems should report parameter magnitudes and bit complexity alongside architecture size.
Constructive proofs can be modularly audited by recording error, width, depth, and weight growth for each subnetwork.
An upper bound for one realization and a lower bound for one construction should never be presented as architecture-wide necessity.
Training-theory bounds that assume bounded parameters need the bound scaled with desired approximation error.
open_questions: What lower bounds characterize the minimum possible ReLU parameter magnitude at an optimal approximation rate?
Can polynomial magnitude be retained without the L-to-L^2 depth increase?
How do quantization and bit complexity change the width-depth-error tradeoff?
Can regularized gradient training recover comparably bounded constructive approximants?
Do path norm or scale-invariant complexity measures yield sharper comparisons than maximum weight?

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Network Approximation for Smooth Functions
competitive_landscape.difference: Establishes the near-optimal width-depth error rate; the reviewed paper modifies its construction and adds explicit polynomial bounds on realizing parameter magnitudes.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Approximation of Functions by Tanh Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Provides high-order Sobolev approximation with two-hidden-layer tanh networks and polynomial weight bounds; the reviewed work focuses on deep ReLU, uniform error, and width-depth joint rates.

competitive_landscape.title: Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Encodable Weights in Smoothness Spaces
competitive_landscape.difference: Derives lower and upper complexity results with encodable weights across smoothness spaces; the reviewed paper gives a sharper maximum-magnitude exponent in many matched C^q regimes but no encodability lower bound.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Network Approximation Characterized by Number of Neurons
competitive_landscape.difference: Characterizes approximation power by neuron count and modulus of continuity; the reviewed work analyzes smooth-function parameter magnitude for a later near-optimal construction.

competitive_landscape.title: Optimal Approximation of Piecewise Smooth Functions using Deep ReLU Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Proves necessary and sufficient architecture complexity for piecewise-smooth targets; the reviewed paper studies numerical magnitude rather than only count and does not establish matching lower bounds.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: A state-of-the-art deep-ReLU approximation rate can be realized with only polynomial parameter growth, often improving existing growth bounds.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The explicit component audit and Theorem 4 provide the polynomial upper bound; Tables 1-2 normalize several prior results, while Theorem 2 gives a construction-specific shallow contrast.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Explicitly tracking parameter magnitudes fills a real gap in constructive approximation theory. The contribution is an upper-bound audit with a depth tradeoff, not an optimal characterization or evidence of trainability.

reviewer_notes: Read all 39 pages, including the explicit network composition, asymptotic comparisons, negative-result proof, and qualifications. Primary arXiv records for competing approximation theorems were checked on 2026-08-23.
